display.label: CloudFront Distribution
display.description: A CloudFront content delivery network distribution in front of S3 buckets (with Origin Access Control), load balancers, or other web origins.

globals.label: AWS Region
globals.description: CloudFront is global, so this only sets where the AWS provider connects. Certificates must still be in us-east-1.

resource.key_description: An identifier for this distribution within the deployment (does not appear in AWS).

sections.label: Basic Settings

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Whether the distribution accepts viewer requests. Turn off to stop serving without deleting the distribution.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: A note to tell this distribution apart in the AWS console. Up to 128 characters.

fields.label: Alternate Domain Names (CNAMEs)
fields.description: Your own domain names for this distribution, such as cdn.example.com. Each needs a matching ACM certificate (see Custom SSL Certificate) and a DNS record pointing at the distribution.

fields.label: Default Root Object
fields.description: Object requested when a viewer requests the root URL, e.g. index.html.

fields.label: Price Class

options.label: Use North America, Europe, Asia, Middle East, and Africa
Use only North America and Europe

fields.description: Which edge locations serve your content. Fewer regions cost less; viewers elsewhere are served from the nearest included location, with more latency.

fields.label: IPv6
fields.description: Answer viewers over IPv6 as well as IPv4. If you alias a Route 53 record to the distribution, add an AAAA record too.

fields.label: Supported HTTP Versions
fields.description: The newest HTTP version viewers may use. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are faster for most browsers; older clients fall back automatically.

fields.label: AWS WAF Web ACL
fields.description: ARN of an AWS WAF web ACL to filter requests. It must be a global (CLOUDFRONT-scope) web ACL, created in us-east-1. Leave empty for none.

sections.description: Identity and delivery settings for the distribution.

sections.label: Origins

fields.label: Origin
Origin Name
fields.description: A name for this origin, unique within the distribution. Cache behaviors and origin groups use it to point here.

fields.label: This is an Amazon S3 bucket origin
fields.description: On for an S3 bucket accessed through its REST endpoint. Off for anything else — a load balancer, a web server, or an S3 static website endpoint, which CloudFront treats as a custom origin.

fields.label: Origin Domain
fields.description: For an S3 origin, the bucket's REST endpoint (pick a bucket, or type <bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com). For a custom origin, the server's domain name.

fields.label: Origin Path
fields.description: A directory in the origin to serve from, starting with / and without a trailing slash, such as /production. Leave empty to serve from the root.

fields.label: Origin Access

options.label: Use an existing Origin Access Control
Use an existing Origin Access Identity (legacy)

fields.description: How CloudFront authenticates to the bucket so it can stay private. Leave empty or choose 'Create' to have an Origin Access Control made for this origin (recommended).

fields.label: Origin Access Control ID
fields.description: ID of an existing Origin Access Control, such as E2QWRUHAPOMQZL.

fields.label: Origin Access Identity
fields.description: Path of an existing Origin Access Identity: origin-access-identity/cloudfront/E1ABCDEF2GHIJ. Legacy; AWS recommends Origin Access Control instead.

fields.label: OAC Request Signing

options.label: Do not override a viewer's Authorization header

fields.description: Used when an Origin Access Control is created. 'Always' signs every request (recommended). 'Never' does not sign. 'Do not override' keeps a viewer's own Authorization header when one is sent.

fields.label: OAC Name
fields.description: Used when an Origin Access Control is created. Must be unique in the account, up to 64 characters. Leave empty for <distribution name>-<origin name>.

fields.label: Grant this distribution read access to the bucket
fields.description: Replace the bucket's policy with one letting only this distribution read objects through Origin Access Control. Turn on only if nothing else sets this bucket's policy, including the S3 module's Bucket Policy field — a bucket has one policy and this overwrites it. Otherwise copy the policy from this deployment's s3_bucket_policies output into the bucket's own policy. KMS-encrypted buckets also need the key policy to allow CloudFront.

fields.label: Protocol
fields.description: How CloudFront connects to the origin. HTTPS Only is recommended; Match Viewer uses the protocol the viewer used.

fields.label: HTTP Port
fields.description: Port the origin listens on for HTTP. Used by HTTP Only and Match Viewer.

fields.label: HTTPS Port
fields.description: Port the origin listens on for HTTPS.

fields.label: Minimum Origin SSL Protocols
fields.description: TLS versions CloudFront may use with the origin over HTTPS, such as TLSv1.2. Older versions only for origins that cannot do better.

fields.label: Custom Headers
fields.description: Headers CloudFront adds to every request it sends to this origin — for example a secret header the origin checks to accept only CloudFront traffic.

fields.label: Connection Attempts
fields.description: How many times CloudFront tries to connect to the origin before failing over or returning an error (1-3).

fields.label: Connection Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: Seconds CloudFront waits to establish a connection to the origin (1-10).

fields.label: Enable Origin Shield
fields.description: Adds a regional caching layer in front of the origin, reducing load on it at extra cost.

fields.label: Origin Shield Region
fields.description: The Origin Shield region; choose the one closest to the origin.
Where CloudFront fetches content from. Add one per bucket or server; cache behaviors and origin groups refer to them by name.

sections.description: The S3 buckets and servers CloudFront fetches content from.

fields.label: Origin Group
fields.description: Pairs a primary and a secondary origin so CloudFront fails over automatically when the primary returns one of the chosen status codes.

fields.label: Origin Group Name
fields.description: A name for this group, unique among origins and groups. Cache behaviors can point at it instead of a single origin.

fields.label: Failover Status Codes
fields.description: Status codes from the primary origin that send the request to the secondary, such as 500, 502, 503 and 504.

fields.label: Primary Origin
fields.description: The origin tried first. Must match an origin name above.

fields.label: Secondary Origin
fields.description: The origin used when the primary fails. Must match an origin name above.

sections.label: Default Cache Behavior

fields.label: Origin
fields.description: The origin or origin group that requests go to when no path-based behavior matches. Must match a name above; it also identifies this distribution in the deployment.

fields.label: Viewer Protocol Policy
fields.description: What CloudFront does with plain HTTP requests from viewers. Redirect to HTTPS is recommended.

fields.label: Allowed HTTP Methods
fields.description: HTTP methods CloudFront accepts and forwards: GET and HEAD for static content; add OPTIONS for CORS; all seven (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) for an API.

fields.label: Cached HTTP Methods
fields.description: Methods whose responses are cached: GET and HEAD, optionally OPTIONS.

fields.label: Compress objects automatically
fields.description: Compress text responses (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON) with gzip or Brotli when the viewer supports it.

fields.label: Cache Policy
fields.description: Controls what is cached and for how long. Defaults to the AWS-managed 'CachingOptimized' policy; use CachingDisabled (4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad) for dynamic content, or the ID of your own policy.

fields.label: Origin Request Policy
fields.description: Which headers, cookies and query strings are sent to the origin beyond those in the cache key. For example AllViewer (216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eafa07d3); not for S3 origins with Origin Access Control, which must not receive the viewer's Host header. Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Response Headers Policy
fields.description: Headers CloudFront adds to responses, such as CORS or security headers. For example SimpleCORS (60669652-455b-4ae9-85a4-c4c02393f86c). Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Field-Level Encryption Config
fields.description: ID of a field-level encryption configuration, to encrypt specific form fields at the edge. Requires HTTPS viewers. Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Real-time Log Configuration
fields.description: ARN of a real-time log configuration that streams request logs to Kinesis Data Streams. Leave empty for none.

sections.description: How requests are handled when no path-based behavior matches.

fields.label: Cache Behavior
fields.description: Different settings for requests whose path matches a pattern, such as /api/*. Checked in this order; the first match wins, and anything unmatched uses the default behavior.

fields.label: Path Pattern
fields.description: The paths this behavior applies to, such as /api/* or *.jpg. Case-sensitive.

fields.label: Origin
fields.description: The origin or origin group requests matching this path go to. Must match a name above.

fields.label: Viewer Protocol Policy
fields.description: What CloudFront does with plain HTTP requests from viewers. Redirect to HTTPS is recommended.

fields.label: Allowed HTTP Methods
fields.description: HTTP methods CloudFront accepts and forwards: GET and HEAD for static content; add OPTIONS for CORS; all seven (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) for an API.

fields.label: Cached HTTP Methods
fields.description: Methods whose responses are cached: GET and HEAD, optionally OPTIONS.

fields.label: Compress objects automatically
fields.description: Compress text responses (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON) with gzip or Brotli when the viewer supports it.

fields.label: Cache Policy
fields.description: Controls what is cached and for how long. Defaults to the AWS-managed 'CachingOptimized' policy; use CachingDisabled (4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad) for dynamic content, or the ID of your own policy.

fields.label: Origin Request Policy
fields.description: Which headers, cookies and query strings are sent to the origin beyond those in the cache key. For example AllViewer (216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eafa07d3); not for S3 origins with Origin Access Control, which must not receive the viewer's Host header. Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Response Headers Policy
fields.description: Headers CloudFront adds to responses, such as CORS or security headers. For example SimpleCORS (60669652-455b-4ae9-85a4-c4c02393f86c). Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Field-Level Encryption Config
fields.description: ID of a field-level encryption configuration, to encrypt specific form fields at the edge. Requires HTTPS viewers. Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Real-time Log Configuration
fields.description: ARN of a real-time log configuration that streams request logs to Kinesis Data Streams. Leave empty for none.

sections.label: Custom SSL Certificate

fields.label: Use the default CloudFront certificate
fields.description: Serve HTTPS on the distribution's *.cloudfront.net name only. Turn off to use your own certificate for the alternate domain names.

fields.label: ACM Certificate
fields.description: An ACM certificate covering every alternate domain name. It must be in us-east-1 — CloudFront only accepts certificates from that region, whatever region is selected above.

fields.label: Security Policy Support
fields.description: SNI Only works for all modern clients at no cost. A dedicated IP supports very old clients and costs extra each month.

fields.label: Security Policy
fields.description: The oldest TLS version viewers may use. TLSv1.2_2021 is recommended; choose older only for clients that need it.

sections.description: HTTPS certificate for the alternate domain names.

sections.label: Geographic Restrictions

fields.label: Restriction Type
fields.description: Limit access by the viewer's country: allow only the listed countries, or block them.

fields.label: Countries
fields.description: Two-letter country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), such as US, GB or IN.

sections.description: Allow or block viewers by country.

sections.label: Standard Logging

fields.label: Enable standard logging
fields.description: Write a log of every viewer request to an S3 bucket.

fields.label: S3 Bucket for Logs
fields.description: The bucket receiving logs, as <bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com. It needs ACLs enabled (Object Ownership not set to 'Bucket owner enforced').

fields.label: Log Prefix
fields.description: A folder for the log files within the bucket, such as cloudfront/. Leave empty for the bucket root.

fields.label: Include cookies in logs
fields.description: Include viewer cookies in the logs.

sections.description: Request logs written to an S3 bucket.

sections.label: Custom Error Responses

fields.label: Custom Error Response
HTTP Error Code
fields.description: The origin's HTTP status to replace, such as 403 or 404.

fields.label: Response HTTP Code
fields.description: The status returned to the viewer instead, such as 200. Leave empty to keep the original.

fields.label: Response Page Path
fields.description: Path of the page to return, such as /errors/404.html or /index.html. It must be reachable through a cache behavior.

fields.label: Error Caching Minimum TTL
fields.description: Seconds CloudFront caches this error before asking the origin again. Leave empty for the default, 10 seconds.
Replace error responses from the origin with your own page or status — for example serve /index.html with 200 for 404s in a single-page app.

sections.description: Your own pages or status codes in place of origin errors.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Key-value tags for cost allocation and organization.

satellites.note: An Origin Access Control is created for each S3 origin set to create one, and deleted with the distribution.
With 'Grant this distribution read access' on, the bucket's whole policy is replaced; deleting the distribution removes it.
